rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.e1: Defence: in an Alekhine Defence game played on Lichess, Black has castled. The pawns on f7 and g7, in front of the king, form the pawn shield.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.e2: The shield takes squares and lines away from the enemy pieces. In positions like this, with queens on the board and enemy pieces near the king, a shield pawn only advances for a concrete defensive reason.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.e3: The queen on h5 and the knight on g5 attack f7, and only the king defends that pawn.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.p: It is Black to play. Find a move that keeps your king protected.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.certo: With that move, your king stays protected. The knight on e5, for example, defends f7, and the shield stays in place.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.revela: A good move was the knight to e5: it defends f7, and the shield stays in place.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g7g6.1: The g7 pawn advances and attacks the queen.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g7g6.2: With this move White has a resource: the queen goes to h7 with check, and the g7 square is now empty.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g7g6.4: The queen captures on f7 along the seventh rank, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate. The g7 pawn used to close that rank.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g7g6.5: Back to the position: look for a move that defends f7 without touching the shield.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g8f8.1: The king goes to f8 to defend f7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g8f8.2: The queen captures on f7, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate: the king alone does not defend f7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.g8f8.3: Back to the position: f7 needs one more defender besides the king.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.e8f8.1: The rook goes to f8 and defends f7, but it takes the king's escape square.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.e8f8.2: The queen goes to h7, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate: f8 is taken by the rook.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.err.e8f8.3: Back to the position: defend f7 without taking the king's escape square.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.fora: That move gives White the advantage. Before choosing, see what the queen on h5 and the knight on g5 attack near your king.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: keep the shield and defend f7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.l1: The knight goes to e5 and defends f7. The shield stays in place, and Black is better.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex1.l2: In the game, Black advanced the g7 pawn to attack the queen, and White gave mate. In positions like this, with queens on the board, attacking a piece is not a reason to touch the shield.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.e1: Defence: now with Black, in another game played on Lichess. The queen on b1 aims at h7 along the diagonal, and the knight on g5 also attacks h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.e2: White threatens to capture the knight on f6 with the knight on d5, with check. After the recapture, the knight on f6 no longer defends h7, and the queen mates on h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.p: Find a move that stops the mate.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.certo: With that move, the mate does not happen. The pawn on g6, for example, closes the queen's diagonal to h7: here the shield pawn advances for a reason.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.revela: A good move was the pawn to g6: it closes the queen's diagonal to h7, and the mate disappears.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.alt.b7d5.1: The bishop captures the knight on d5, which would give the check on f6. That works too.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.alt.b7d5.2: Another good move is the pawn to g6, which closes the queen's diagonal to h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.h7h6.1: The h7 pawn advances and attacks the knight on g5.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.h7h6.2: With this move White has a resource: the knight on d5 captures on f6 with check.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.h7h6.4: The queen goes to h7, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate. The advance did not close the diagonal: it only opened the h7 square.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.h7h6.5: Back to the position: look for a move that closes the queen's diagonal to h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.f6d5.1: The knight on f6 captures on d5 and stops defending h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.f6d5.2: The queen captures on h7, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.f6d5.3: Back to the position: the knight on f6 must stay near the king. Close the queen's diagonal to h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.c5c4.1: The c5 pawn advances, far from the king.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.c5c4.2: The knight on d5 captures on f6 with check.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.c5c4.3: The g7 pawn recaptures, and h7 is left without a defender.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.c5c4.4: The queen captures on h7, supported by the knight on g5, and gives mate.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.err.c5c4.5: Back to the position: the threat is near the king. Close the queen's diagonal to h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not stop the threat: the knight captures on f6 with check, and White gives mate or wins material. Look for a move that closes the queen's diagonal to h7.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: close the queen's diagonal.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.l1: The g7 pawn goes to g6 and cuts the diagonal. Without the mate on h7, Black is better.
rot.kingSafety.ideia.ex2.l2: In the game, Black advanced the h7 pawn to attack the knight and got mated. In positions like this, with queens on, a shield pawn advances to close a line of attack or open an escape square.
rot.kingSafety.demos.alekhine.1: Defence: now with Black, in an Alekhine Defence game played on Lichess. The queen on f3, the knight on g5 and the pawn on e6 attack f7.
rot.kingSafety.demos.alekhine.2: If the white queen goes to f7 with check, the black queen captures her, and the e6 pawn recaptures on f7 with mate: the king has no free square.
rot.kingSafety.demos.alekhine.3: The g7 pawn advances one square and opens g7 for the king. After the exchanges on f7, the king escapes via g7.
rot.kingSafety.demos.alekhine.4: White castles: without the mate, the attack has lost its force, and Black is better. Here the shield pawn advanced for a reason: to open an escape square.
rot.kingSafety.demos.caroKann.1: Attack: now with White, in a Caro-Kann game played on Lichess. The f7 pawn has already left, and the bishop on c4 watches g8. The rook on h3 aims at h7.
rot.kingSafety.demos.caroKann.2: The rook captures the pawn on h7 with check.
rot.kingSafety.demos.caroKann.3: The king captures the rook, because g8 is watched by the bishop on c4.
rot.kingSafety.demos.caroKann.4: The queen goes to h5 and gives mate. The bishop watches g8, the queen watches g6 and h6, and the g7 pawn takes the last square from its own king.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.1: Defence: now with Black, in the Berlin Defence, which Kasparov and Kramnik played in London in 2000. The queens are off, and the black king is on d8, without castling.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.2: In positions like this, without queens and with no enemy pieces near the king, the king in the centre runs little risk: there is not enough force for a mating attack. Here is a possible continuation.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.4: The bishop develops and frees c8 for the king.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.5: The b2 pawn advances and prepares the c1 bishop's move to b2.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.6: The h7 pawn advances and takes the g5 square away from the white knight and bishop.
rot.kingSafety.demos.berlim.8: The king goes to c8, behind the pawns on b7 and c7. The position stays balanced: without queens, the uncastled king is safe and, in the endgame, can go to the centre and join the game.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Now with White, in a pawn endgame played on Lichess. The queens left the board long ago. Is it worth keeping the king behind the pawns, protected? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The king went to the centre and attacks the pawn on e4. In a pawn endgame, without queens, the king needs no shield: it attacks and defends like the other pieces.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.f2f4: The pawn advanced, but the king stayed behind the pawns, away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. Bring the king to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3h4: The king stayed away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. In the endgame, without queens, the king is an attacking piece: bring it to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3h3: The king stayed away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. In the endgame, without queens, the king is an attacking piece: bring it to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3g2: The king stayed away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. In the endgame, without queens, the king is an attacking piece: bring it to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.f2f3: The pawn advanced, but the king stayed behind the pawns, away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. Bring the king to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.h2h3: The pawn advanced, but the king stayed behind the pawns, away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. Bring the king to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.valeAqui.err.h2h4: The pawn advanced, but the king stayed behind the pawns, away from the centre, and the black king reaches the white pawns first. Bring the king to the centre.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.escudo.enunciado: Now with White, in a game played on Lichess. The knight on g4 attacks h2, and the knight on e5 can leave with check on f3 and open the c7 queen's diagonal to h2. Play as White and protect your king.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.escudo.fim: Your king stayed protected: the shield stayed in place, and the black queen can no longer mate on h2.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.escudo.err.h2h3: The h2 pawn advances and attacks the knight, but the other knight captures on f3 with check, the white queen recaptures, and the black queen mates on h2. Attacking a piece is not a reason to touch the shield.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.escudo.err.a2a3: The a2 pawn attacks the bishop, far from the king. The knight on e5 captures on f3 with check, the g2 pawn recaptures, and the queen mates on h2. First, deal with the threat near the king.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.escudo.err.d1e2: The queen leaves d1, but the knight on e5 captures on f3 with check, the g2 pawn recaptures, and the black queen mates on h2. First, deal with the threat near the king.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.diagonal.enunciad: Now with White, in a Caro-Kann game. The bishop on d6, the knight on g4 and the queen on c7 aim at h2. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.diagonal.fim: The g3 pawn closed the bishop's diagonal to h2. Here the shield pawn advanced for a reason: to close a line of attack.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.diagonal.err.h2h3: The h2 pawn advances and attacks the knight, but the bishop gives check on h2, the knight on f3 captures, and the queen mates on h2. Close the bishop's diagonal.
rot.kingSafety.pratica.diagonal.err.c4c5: The c4 pawn advances and attacks the bishop, but the bishop gives check on h2, the knight on f3 captures, and the queen mates on h2. Close the bishop's diagonal.
